today.h: The 10Y Hits 5.34%, Then Blinks: S&P Snaps a 3-Day Slide to Open Q4
today.c1: October opened with a full risk cycle in one session: the 10Y spiked to 5.344% — its highest since April 2002 — on a hot ISM prices gauge, dragging the Dow down about 200 points early; by late morning, yields blinked. The 2Y tumbled 10bp to 4.79% and the 10Y retreated to 5.24%, and stocks followed bonds up: the S&P closed +0.19% at 7,666.45, snapping a three-day slide. Energy (+1.9%) led on China's fuel-export halt and a third US carrier group bound for the Middle East; Micron (+3%) and Accenture (+16%) carried tech; Nike fell 5% after hours on light guidance. Friday's payrolls are the next referee.
today.c4:
• Rates are the pilot and Friday's payrolls are the judge: 5.34% marked the ceiling on the 10Y — a hot jobs number re-tests it, a soft one extends the relief trade.
  • Respect the fuel tape: China's export halt plus a third carrier keep Brent's war premium live above $100 — energy leads when escalation bites, and feeds the Fed's problem when it doesn't retreat.
  • Earnings get paid only with proof: Accenture +16% (bookings $22.2B) vs Micron's grudging +3% and Nike's -5% after hours — demand evidence is the price of admission.

chains.t: ① Main Chain: The 10Y's 24-Year High — and the First Yield Pullback in a Week
steps: 10Y spikes to 5.344% — highest since April 2002 — after the ISM prices gauge jumps to 77.9
30Y touches fresh 24-year highs; the global long end sells off with it (UK 30Y gilt at 6%)
The Dow slides about 200 points early as the high re-prices everything
Late morning: yields buckle — 2Y -10bp, 10Y -5bp; a seven-day rising streak snaps
Bonds lead, stocks follow: S&P claws from red to +0.19% at 7,666.45
chains.d: The day's whole shape came from the long end: a 24-year-high print in the 10Y dragged stocks down, and the first yield pullback in a week dragged them back up.

news.fact: The 10Y hit an intraday 5.344%, its highest since April 3, 2002; the 30Y scaled 24-year highs as global bonds sold off.
ISM manufacturing held at 54.5 but the prices-paid gauge surged 6.8 points to 77.9 — the inflation fear that pushed yields up.
Yields turned by late morning: the 2Y fell 10bp to 4.79% and the 10Y to ~5.24% — snapping a seven-day streak of rising yields.
'There's some fatigue in the bond market... a little optimism that this is going to be a short-lived move to 5%,' said KKM Financial's Jeff Kilburg.
Stocks snapped a three-day slide: S&P +0.19% at 7,666.45; the Nasdaq rose for a second straight day.

chains.t: ② Oil's Second Shock: China Halts Fuel Exports, a Third Carrier Sails
steps: Morning dip: Mideast crude flows had recovered, capping the fear premium
Reuters: China suspends October fuel exports beyond HK/Macau; PetroChina cancels cargoes
WSJ: a third US carrier strike group — up to 10,000 troops — due by end-November
WTI settles +2.7% at $92.87; Brent +4.4% to $102.31
Refiners ride it: Marathon +5.7%, Valero +5%; energy is the day's best sector
chains.d: The war premium found two fresh bids — China's export ban and a new carrier deployment — lifting Brent back over $102 while the rest of the tape stayed flat.

news.fact: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau; PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes as Beijing prioritized domestic supply.
Oil extended gains after the WSJ reported a third US carrier strike group will arrive by end-November, with up to 10,000 additional troops.
WTI settled +2.7% at $92.87; Brent jumped 4.4% to $102.31 — the day's cleanest one-way trade.
Refining margins flashed: Marathon Petroleum +5.7% and Valero +5% led the energy complex.

chains.t: ③ Proof of Earnings: Accenture +16%, Synopsys +10% — Micron's Grudging +3%
steps: Accenture soars 16% on an FQ4 beat: EPS $3.29, revenue $18.7B, bookings $22.2B
Micron erases losses to end +3% — a record quarter, but 'a high burden' on the stock
Synopsys +10% on OpenAI and Amazon custom-chip deals (Amazon pact worth over $1B)
Memory complex rallies with it: DRAM ETF +3%, SK Hynix +5%
Tech +1.1% and the Nasdaq's second straight up day — even as the tape stayed flat
chains.d: Beneath a flat index the AI complex flexed: three blowout prints showed demand proof still gets paid — selectivity is the premium.

news.fact: Accenture paced the S&P at +16%: Q4 EPS $3.29 (est $3.19), revenue +6% to $18.68B, bookings $22.17B — with a raised outlook and dividend.
Micron closed up 3% after its record quarter: the stock has 'nearly quadrupled in value this year,' and investors 'are putting a high burden' on it, Gabelli's Hendi Susanto said.
Synopsys jumped 10% after announcing AI deals with OpenAI (a joint chip-design model) and Amazon (custom silicon, worth over $1B).
The Nasdaq's second straight gain came as 'Wall Street piled back into AI stocks after Micron's earnings report.'

chains.t: ④ Under the Flat Tape: 6 of 11 Sectors Fell — a Rotation, Not a Rally
steps: Indexes green, but 6 of 11 S&P sectors closed red
Energy +1.9% and Tech +1.1% carried the tape; Health Care -1.3% was worst
Russell 2000 +0.35% outperformed — the day after a ~7.5% quarter
Bespoke: September equal-weight lagged cap-weight by 4.6pp — 3rd-worst month since 2003
Single names: FICO +8%, Mattel +19%, MSG Sports -5%, McCormick -5%
chains.d: The +0.19% headline hid a rotate-under-the-hood day: fuel and AI up, defensives and health care down — the same split September ran on.

news.fact: Health Care (-1.3%) and Communication Services (-0.9%) were the drags while Energy (+1.9%) led; six of eleven sectors ended red.
Bespoke: the equal-weight S&P trailed the cap-weighted index by 4.6pp in September — a historic month of underperformance for breadth.
Small caps: the Russell 2000 outperformed Thursday (+0.35%) after a ~7.5% third-quarter decline, still up more than 12% in 2026.
FICO +8% (FHFA's Pulte backs FICO Direct), Mattel +19% (WSJ: takeover interest from Authentic Brands), MSG Sports -5% (board approves Knicks-Rangers split), McCormick -5%.

chains.t: ⑤ Late-Cycle Check: Fed Speak Points to a Pause; Nike -5% Frames Q4 Earnings
steps: Jefferson: future policy adjustments 'may take more time'; Williams: 'no need for urgency'
October hike odds slide to ~31% (from 38% intraday, 69% a week ago)
Claims 197k — third week below 200k; Challenger layoffs lowest since 2022
Friday's payrolls (~85k expected) are the next repricing trigger
After close: Nike -5% on a light FY27 guide (EPS $1.15-1.35 vs ~$1.65 street)
chains.d: The dovish undercurrent is the day's quiet story — hike odds slid all week — while Nike's after-hours miss warns that not every Q4 print will look like Accenture's.

news.fact: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said adjustments 'may take more time'; NY Fed's Williams said there is 'no need for urgency' — the Street reads a nearing pause in hikes.
October hike odds fell to ~31%, down from 45% before Wednesday's PCE and 69% a week earlier; December is still fully priced.
Jobless claims 197k — below the 200k consensus; Challenger: September layoffs 43,281, with year-to-date plans lowest since 2022.
Nike -5% after hours: adjusted EPS $0.48 beat (~$0.44 est) but revenue missed ($11.21B) and FY27 EPS guidance ($1.15-1.35) landed far below the ~$1.65 street.
September payrolls due Friday — estimates cluster around 84k-90k (Dow Jones 84k / FactSet 90k), unemployment seen at 4.1%.

mtd.h: October Starts Split: +0.19% as Yields Retreat From 24-Year Highs; Brent Re-Tests $102
mtd.d: S&P 7,651.5 to 7,666.5 on day one (+0.19%): October's three forces — a 5%-plus 10Y, $100-plus Brent, demands for earnings proof — are all still in play.
mtd.c1: One session into October, the market has resolved nothing — which is the point. The month opened with the 10Y at a 24-year high — before its seven-day rise snapped; Brent pushed back over $100 on China's fuel-export halt; and the AI complex showed its two faces — Accenture (+16%) got paid, Micron (+3%) barely did. Net for day one: +0.19%, six of eleven sectors red, small caps ahead: a rotation month wearing a flat index as a disguise.
mtd.c4:
• October's checkpoint list: Friday's payrolls, the late-October Fed meeting and the Q3 earnings wave — each can re-price the 10Y's 5.2% shelf.
  • Watch the fuel channel: China's export stop and the third carrier give Brent a live bid; an actual Iran resolution remains the single biggest downside risk to the inflation tape.
  • Breadth: equal-weight lagged by 4.6pp in September — the broadening trade starts working only when oil stops leading.

chains.t: ① October's Opening Setup: Rates, Fuel, Earnings — All at Extremes
steps: October opens with the 10Y at 5.24%, one day off 24-year highs
Brent back over $100 on China's export halt and a third carrier
AI demand remains the market's dependable bid (Accenture, Micron, Synopsys)
Day one nets +0.19% — the month's path is the sum of those three
Friday's payrolls are the first referee
chains.d: October opens with all three of its swing factors — the long end, the war's fuel premium, earnings proof — at decision points; day one resolved them to +0.19%.

news.fact: The 10Y posted its biggest quarterly rise this century in July-September (+87bp) and opened Q4 at 5.24% after touching 5.344%.
China suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong/Macau, tightening the war-constrained product market further.
Payrolls preview: roughly 84k-90k expected for September, with unemployment seen at 4.1%.

chains.t: ② The Repricing in Slow Motion: Hike Odds 69% to 31% in a Week
steps: A week ago: October hike odds near 69%
Soft August PCE (9/30) and dovish Fed voices cut them to ~38%
By Thursday's close: ~31% — the October hike trade is fading
December is still fully priced — a repricing, not a pivot
Payrolls Friday decides the next leg
chains.d: The month's most important move may be in the odds, not the tape: an October hike that was 69% priced last week is down to ~31%.

news.fact: October hike probability slid to ~31%, from 45% before the PCE report and 69% a week earlier, after softer inflation data.
Jefferson: policy adjustments 'may take more time'; Williams earlier in the week: 'no need for urgency.'

chains.t: ③ The Breadth Ledger: September's 4.6pp Warning for October
steps: September: equal-weight trailed cap-weight by 4.6pp — third-worst month since 2003
Small caps fell ~7.5% in Q3 — yet sit +13% YTD
Day one: Russell outperformed, Energy led, Health Care lagged
Bespoke: the broadening trade needs lower oil prices first
October's question: does the rotation get a sequel?
chains.d: September's damage was underneath the index — equal-weight's 4.6pp lag — and October's first day kept the same cross-section: fuel and AI up, defensives down.

news.fact: Bespoke flagged September as a historic month of equal-weight underperformance; the RSP trailed SPY by 4.6pp.
The Russell 2000 outperformed Thursday after a ~7.5% third-quarter decline; it remains up more than 12% in 2026.

qtd.h: Q4 Opens on the Q3 Fault Line: +0.19% as Micron Recharges the AI Bid
qtd.d: 9/30 7,651.5 to 10/1 7,666.5 (+0.19%): the quarter opens with Q3's unresolved fight — an earnings-proof AI complex against a 5%-plus long bond — still even.
qtd.c1: Q4's first session looked like Q3's last: the long end tried to break something (a 5.344% print on the 10Y) and the AI complex refused to break (Micron +3%, Accenture +16%, Synopsys +10%). In between, the quarter opens nearly flat — +0.19% — carrying Q3's three questions: can earnings outrun rates, can the war's fuel premium be capped, and does breadth ever widen. Gold's +0.4% and a dollar at a three-month high round out the macro set.
qtd.c4:
• Q4's trade starts where Q3's ended: own proven AI demand, rent the rest — Micron's 'high burden' and Nike's -5% after hours show the ledge is narrow.
  • The 10Y's 5.2% is the valuation ceiling and 5.34% its stress test — Friday's payrolls is the next trial.
  • Energy is Q4's macro wildcard: the third carrier deployment gives the war premium a November deadline — hedge the fuel tail.

chains.t: ① The Q3 Handoff: +2% to Defend and a 5.2% Yield to Beat
steps: The spoiler: the 10Y's +87bp — the biggest quarterly rise this century
Q4 day one: +0.19%, with the 10Y 5bp off 24-year highs
Now earnings season's turn to carry the load
AI prints set the early tone (Micron, Accenture)
chains.d: Q3 ended net-positive but rate-taxed; Q4 opens on the same arithmetic — earnings must outrun the long bond.

news.fact: Q3 closed with the S&P up 2.03% and the Nasdaq up 2.47% — a second straight quarterly gain — while the Dow fell 2.70%.
The 10Y posted its biggest quarterly rise this century in July-September.

chains.t: ② The Global Long End: a Worldwide Repricing, Not a US Story
steps: US 30Y at fresh 24-year highs; the 10Y touched 5.344%
UK 30Y gilt yields hit 6% — their highest since February 1998
Japan and euro-area long bonds sold off in sympathy
The dollar rose to a three-month high as the US out-yields peers
Q4's stability question starts with global duration
chains.d: The rate shock is global: a UK 30-year gilt at 6% and a 24-year-high US long end say the repricing is about debt and inflation everywhere.

news.fact: UK 30-year gilt yields hit 6%, their highest since February 1998, as a global bond selloff deepened.
The dollar climbed to a three-month high against a basket of peers as US yields stayed above the rest of the world's.

chains.t: ③ Fuel as the Quarter's Inflation Input: $100 Brent Re-Tested
steps: Q3: WTI +30% as the war premium rebuilt
Q4 day one: China halts October fuel exports; Brent +4.4% over $102
A third US carrier group due by end-November
Refiners lead again (Marathon +5.7%, Valero +5%)
Wall Street's 2026 Brent forecasts keep rising (Reuters poll: $89 average)
chains.d: Oil re-entered Q4 the same way it dominated Q3 — through supply fear, not demand — and fuel is once again the quarter's fastest inflation input.

news.fact: China's refiners suspended October fuel exports; PetroChina cancelled cargoes as Beijing prioritized domestic supply.
Reuters' monthly poll lifted the 2026 Brent forecast to $89.05/b (from $85.08) with WTI at $83.90, as Gulf disruption drags on.

ytd.h: The Bull Holds Into Q4: S&P +11.99% as the 10Y's +108bp Rewrites the Playbook
ytd.d: S&P +11.99%, Nasdaq +15.62%, Dow +5.96% through three quarters and day one of Q4 — AI and earnings carried; the 10Y's +108bp and an eighth month of war taxed the rest.
ytd.c1: Three quarters and a day in: the bull market still runs on AI capex and earnings, and still fights the same two taxes — a 10Y up 108bp this year to 5.24%, and oil up about 62% as the war crossed into an eighth month. The record books: S&P +11.99%, Nasdaq +15.62%, Dow +5.96%; underneath, energy and tech lead while the consumer, utilities and long duration lag. Q4 opened with a +0.19% nod and a Nike warning — the pattern of the year: pay for proof, tax the rest.
ytd.c4:
• The year's lesson: buy where earnings compound (AI capex), rent where rates rule (long duration, real estate, the consumer).
  • Rates: the 10Y's +108bp is 2026's biggest tax — a genuine Fed pause would be the largest single bullish catalyst left this year.
  • Wildcards into year-end: the war's fuel premium (month eight) and December's Fed — both live.

steps: AI capex remains the engine (Micron, Nvidia, Synopsys)
Every yield spike has been bought — Thursday's included
Q4 opens at the same place: +0.19%
chains.d: The year's base case hasn't broken: earnings-proof AI compounds, dips get bought, and the S&P sits +11.99% with a quarter to go.

news.fact: The S&P's three-day slide snapped to open Q4; the index enters the quarter +11.99% YTD.
Micron has 'nearly quadrupled' in value this year on AI memory demand — its prints set the tone for the complex.

steps: A war-driven oil shock (WTI ~+62%) re-fed inflation through 2026
The Fed hiked in September; December is still priced
Gold is down ~3% YTD despite the panic — rates dominated
chains.d: 2026's inflation wave came from the barrel, not the printing press: oil and the war re-anchored rate expectations higher all year.

news.fact: October hike odds slid to ~31% after a week that began near 69%; December remains fully priced — inflation fear is still the regime.
Gold fell over 6% in September despite its safe-haven role — rates remained the dominant force for the metal.

steps: Micron nearly quadrupled YTD as the memory shortage let prices run
Deals keep stacking: Synopsys-OpenAI/Amazon, Anthropic, World Labs
Capex is the market's core religion into Q4
chains.d: AI infrastructure remains 2026's compounding machine — chips, memory and design tools all printing demand — and the market pays for it by the billion.

news.fact: Micron's record quarter and Synopsys' $1B+ Amazon silicon pact extended the AI build-out trade into Q4.
Micron 'has already nearly quadrupled in value this year' as the global memory shortage allowed it to raise prices.

steps: The war enters its eighth month with no resolution
The Strait's risk premium is the year's constant: WTI ~+62%
China's fuel-export halt shows the war's second-order shocks
A third US carrier group is due by end-November
chains.d: 2026's hidden tax is geography: eight months of war that re-price oil, bonds and the dollar every time they escalate.

news.fact: A third US carrier strike group (up to 10,000 troops) will arrive by end-November — the war's next visible deadline.
China's October fuel-export suspension is the latest supply squeeze of a war now in its eighth month.

steps: Rates: from cut-hopes in January to hike-odds in October
The dollar is +3.8% YTD at a three-month high as the US out-yields peers
The Fed hiked in September; pause talk is only just returning
December's meeting remains the year's final macro gate
chains.d: 2026 flipped the monetary script — the year started pricing cuts and now prices hikes; the dollar (+3.8%) and gold (-3.2%) both carry the marks.

news.fact: The dollar hit a three-month high as US yields (10Y 5.24%) towered over peers' — the year's regime in one line.
The 10Y is +108bp on the year, including the biggest quarterly rise this century (Q3).
